title: SGLang NCCL weight broadcast -- T1041 no-API-key deployment lets a remote caller exfiltrate all model weights
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-15978 (GHSA-cpqq-22v3-2wfm,
CVSS 7.5 HIGH), affecting SGLang.

When no API key is configured, SGLang exposes TWO endpoints that,
called in sequence by a remote caller, trigger DISTRIBUTED weight
broadcasting over NCCL (the GPU-to-GPU collective communication
library normally used internally for multi-GPU inference) and then
trigger a data transfer -- letting an attacker exfiltrate the entire
served model's weights over what is meant to be an internal,
trusted-cluster communication channel. This is a distinct failure mode
from the pickle-deserialization RCEs in the same disclosure series:
no deserialization bug is needed, only the absence of the API-key
gate that was meant to protect these two endpoints.

Detection logic flags the specific two-call sequence this exfiltration
path depends on: a request to the weight-broadcast-trigger endpoint
followed shortly by a request to the corresponding data-transfer
endpoint, from the same caller, on a deployment where no API key
authentication is configured -- either call alone is unremarkable
internal-cluster traffic, but the pairing from an external caller is
the exfiltration chain this advisory describes.

Aggregated from 2 independent sources (SGLang's own GHSA advisory + an
independent security researcher's corroborating disclosure write-up,
part of the same coordinated multi-CVE SGLang research series), no
patched version confirmed in the summary available at authoring time --
operators should always configure an API key even on deployments
believed to be internal-only.
